subject: a huge moth clinging to the cracked glass housing of an old iron street lamp, seen close so the lamp and the moth fill the whole frame, with the mass of a dead hedge and dry seed heads and tangled bare twigs crowding in on every side and into the near foreground, the moth's wings spread wide and worked all over with fine scaled patterning, and set into that patterning not eyespots but small pale human skulls and rows of tiny teeth and a scatter of thin bones, the lamp's broken head filled with a hot saturated magenta light, deep pink and violet shading to crimson, by far the brightest thing in the picture, that light pouring out from behind the moth and throwing its wings and the twigs and dozens of smaller moths behind it into silhouette, a drift of torn wings and dry insect husks heaped on the lamp's rim and scattered across the twigs below
